basis.saw: Fig. 1, a horizontal timeline from 2004 to 2023 showing key global health workforce milestones, resolutions, and NHWA publications

labels: Final report of the expert group
Final report of the expert group

narrative.text: Fig. 1, ‘Timeline for HWF information strengthening – initiatives, resolutions and publications’. A horizontal timeline spanning 2004 to 2023 with milestone callouts above and below the axis: 2004 (Joint Learning Initiative report published); 2006 (World health report 2006 published; Global health workforce statistics database established); 2009 (Handbook on monitoring and evaluation of human resources for health published); 2010 (WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, WHA63.16); 2013 (Recife report ‘A universal truth: no health without a health workforce’ published); 2016 (Final report of the expert group to the High-Level Commission on Health Employment and Economic Growth published; Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030, WHA69.19); 2017 (NHWA handbook published; NHWA data platform launched); 2018 (NHWA implementation guide published); 2020 (NHWA data portal launched); 2022 (Handbook on strengthening health workforce collection, analysis and use published); and 2023 (NHWA handbook second edition published).

basis.saw: Fig. 4, a 100% stacked horizontal bar chart of the share of countries by number of available NHWA indicators and sub-indicators across global, WHO regional, and World Bank income groups

narrative.text: Fig. 4, ‘Share of countries by the number of indicators and sub-indicators for which data is available on the NHWA data platform’ (Source: WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025). A 100% stacked horizontal bar chart across six categories (10 or less, 11 to 20, 21 to 30, 31 to 40, 41 to 50, and 51 or more indicators/sub-indicators) for Global, the six WHO regions (AFR, AMR, SEAR, EUR, EMR, WPR), and the four World Bank income groups (HIC, UMIC, LMIC, LIC). Globally, 4% of countries have data for 10 or fewer indicators/sub-indicators, 27% for 11 to 20, 21% for 21 to 30, 12% for 31 to 40, 27% for 41 to 50, and 9% for 51 or more.

basis.saw: Fig. 5, a 100% stacked horizontal bar chart of the share of countries by number of occupations with stock data available on the NHWA platform

narrative.text: Fig. 5, ‘Share of countries by the number of occupations for which stock data is available on the NHWA data platform’ (Source: WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025). A 100% stacked horizontal bar chart across five categories (5 or less occupations, 6 to 10, 11 to 20, 21 to 30, and 31 or more occupations) for Global, the six WHO regions (AFR, AMR, SEAR, EUR, EMR, WPR), and the four World Bank income groups (HIC, UMIC, LMIC, LIC). Globally, 1% of countries have stock data for 5 or fewer occupations, 21% for 6 to 10, 29% for 11 to 20, 29% for 21 to 30, and 21% for 31 or more occupations.

basis.saw: Fig. 6, a 100% stacked horizontal bar chart of the share of countries by number of SDG 3.c.1 occupations with stock data reported in 2020–2024

narrative.text: Fig. 6, ‘Share of countries by the number of SDG 3.c.1 occupations for which stock data are available on the NHWA data platform in the last five years (2020–2024)’ (Source: WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025). A 100% stacked horizontal bar chart showing the distribution across five categories (No occupation, 1 occupation, 2 occupations, 3 occupations, and All occupations — medical doctors, nursing and midwifery personnel, dentists, and pharmacists) for Global, WHO regions (AFR, AMR, SEAR, EUR, EMR, WPR), and World Bank income groups (HIC, UMIC, LMIC, LIC). Globally, 84% of countries reported stock data for all four SDG 3.c.1 occupations in 2020–2024 (6% for 3, 4% for 2, 5% for 1, and 3% for none), ranging regionally from 69% in AMR to 94% in AFR.

basis.saw: Fig. 7, a 100% stacked horizontal bar chart of the share of countries by number of years in 2020–2024 with SDG 3.c.1 stock data available

narrative.text: Fig. 7, ‘Share of countries by the number of years out of the last five years (2020–2024) for which stock data for SDG 3.c.1 occupations are available on the NHWA data platform’ (Source: WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025). A 100% stacked horizontal bar chart across six categories (No year, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years, 4 years, and All 5 years) for Global, WHO regions (AFR, AMR, SEAR, EUR, EMR, WPR), and World Bank income groups (HIC, UMIC, LMIC, LIC). Globally, 25% of countries reported data for all 5 years, 33% for 4 years, 14% for 3 years, 13% for 2 years, 12% for 1 year, and 3% for no year.

narrative.text: Fig. 8, ‘Evolution of stock data availability for SDG 3.c.1 occupations between the 2018 GHO data release and the 2025 NHWA data release’ (Source: WHO Global Health Workforce Statistics, 2018; WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025). A rotated multi-series bar chart plotting the number of countries (0 to 200) with stock data available for each year from 1990 to 2024 across the four SDG 3.c.1 occupations (medical doctors, nursing and midwifery personnel, dentists, and pharmacists), contrasting baseline availability in the 2018 GHO release with the additional countries gained in the 2025 NHWA data release.

basis.saw: Fig. 9, a horizontal bar chart showing the number and percentage of Member States with data available across ten key health workforce topics

narrative.text: Fig. 9, ‘Status of data availability for key HWF topics’ (Source: WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025). A horizontal bar chart ranking ten health workforce topics by the number and percentage of WHO Member States reporting data for at least one occupation: Stock (194, 100%), Sex (189, 97%), Activity level (183, 94%), Age group (174, 90%), Graduates (167, 86%), Place of training (139, 72%), Facility ownership (137, 71%), Place of birth (134, 69%), Facility type (131, 68%), and Subnational distribution (85, 44%).

basis.saw: Fig. 10, a stacked vertical bar chart of the cumulative volume of data points across nine key HWF topics by data release year from 2018 to 2025

narrative.text: Fig. 10, ‘Trend of data volume for key HWF topics in the NHWA data platform by year of data release’. A stacked vertical bar chart showing total data points (vertical axis 0 to 300 000) across annual releases from 2018 to 2025, broken down by nine topics: Stock, Activity level, Sex, Age group, Place of birth, Place of training, Facility ownership, Facility type, and Graduates. Total volume grows nearly 20-fold from 12 587 data points in 2018 (stock data only) to 248 873 data points in 2025 across all nine topics.

basis.saw: Fig. 16, a stacked horizontal age-pyramid bar chart showing 2024 population size in thousands by five-year age group and World Bank income group

narrative.text: Fig. 16, ‘Age population pyramid by World Bank income group in 2024, expressed as population size in 1000s by income group’ (Source: UN World Population Prospects 2024). A horizontal stacked bar chart plotting five-year age cohorts from 0–4 up to 100+ against population size in thousands (0 to 350 000 on each side), disaggregated into Low-income, Lower-middle-income, Upper-middle-income, and High-income countries (World Bank FY 2026 classification).

basis.saw: Fig. 17, a two-panel grouped horizontal bar chart showing the age distribution of (a) medical doctors and (b) nursing personnel across six age brackets by World Bank income group

narrative.text: Fig. 17, ‘Age distribution of (a) medical doctors and (b) nursing personnel, by income group’ (Source: WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025, latest available data for 122 countries for medical doctors and 142 countries for nursing personnel over 2015–2024). Two grouped horizontal bar charts showing the percentage of the workforce in six age brackets (<25, 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, 55–64, and 65+) across Low-income, Lower-middle-income, Upper-middle-income, and High-income countries for (a) medical doctors (0.0% to 50.0% scale) and (b) nursing personnel (0.0% to 50.0% scale).

basis.saw: Fig. 18, a two-panel scatter plot comparing the percentage aged under 35 against the percentage aged 55 and over for (a) medical doctors and (b) nursing personnel by country income group

narrative.text: Fig. 18, ‘Relative proportions of (a) medical doctors and (b) nursing personnel aged over 55 years and below 35 years, by income group’ (Source: WHO National Health Workforce Accounts, 2025, latest available data over 2015–2024). Two scatter plots — panel (a) for medical doctors and panel (b) for nursing personnel — plotting each country’s percentage aged <35 on the horizontal axis (0% to 80%) against its percentage aged 55+ on the vertical axis (0% to 60%), colour-coded by World Bank FY 2026 income group (Low-income, Lower-middle-income, Upper-middle-income, and High-income countries), with a diagonal equality line indicating where the share of workers near retirement (55+) equals the share of young workers (<35).
